Heard learned counsel for the parties on the Leave to Appeal Application.

2. The State, by way of present application, has sought leave to file appeal against the judgment and order dated 02.04.2022, passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge/F.T.C./ Special Judge (POCSO), Udham Singh Nagar, in Special Session Trial No. 252 of 2018, State Vs. Rahul Vishwas,
whereby the said Court has acquitted the respondent-accused for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376, 342 of the IPC and under Section 5(l)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter to be referred to as 'the Act').
3. Facts, sans unnecessary details, are that a report was given by the father of victim at Police Station Dineshpur on 23.11.2017 with the averments that at about 07:00 PM of 22.11.2017, minor daughter of informant, aged about 15 years, went missing.

sentences.text: While searching for her daughter, the informant came to know that the respondent-accused had enticed away his daughter.
Hence, it was requested to lodge the report.
4. On the basis of said report, the case was registered against the accused at P.S. Dineshpur on 23.11.2017, under Sections 363 and 366 of IPC.
The matter was investigated.
The site plan was prepared and statements of witnesses were recorded.

sentences.text:
5. After supplying the papers of prosecution to the respondent-accused under Section 207 Cr.P.C.,
the case was committed to the Court of Sessions.

On 04.09.2018, charges under Sections 363, 366,
376 and 342 of IPC and Section 5(l)/6 of the Act were framed against the accused, to which the accused denied and claimed to be tried.

6. The prosecution, in order to prove its case, has produced witnesses PW-1 victim, PW-2 Vichitra Rani Rai, Principal, PW-3 Dr. Divanshi Mittal, PW-4 father of victim and informant, PW-5 Constable Jeevan Kumar and PW-6 S.I. sunil Singh, in the Court.
7. Thereafter, the statement of accused was recorded under Section 313 of Cr.P.C., in which, he denied the occurrence and stated that the case has been preceded falsely against him.
It was also stated by the accused that on the date of occurrence, the victim was major.
8. On completion of trial, the trial Court proceeded to acquit the accused for the charges levelled against him.
9. Assailing the judgment and order of acquittal, the present appeal alongwith leave to appeal application, has been filed by the State before this Court.
10. Learned Deputy Advocate General appearing for the State has argued that the trial court has erred into laws, in recording the judgment of acquittal.
It was also argued that the case against the accused was proved by the prosecution beyond all reasonable doubt.
The witnesses produced on behalf of the prosecution have fully supported the prosecution case.
Therefore, the judgment of the trial court deserves to be set aside.

11. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the accused, while supporting the judgment of the learned trial court, has argued that due to the contradictions in the statements of prosecution witnesses, and there being inconsistency in the deposition of PW-1 victim, the prosecution has failed to prove its case against the respondent.
12. In this matter, the victim was examined as PW-1 in the Court.
She has deposed that on 22.11.2017, the accused took her at some place, however, she does not know, as to which place was that.
On that day, the accused established physical relations with her, however, the relations were established with her consent.

She has also stated in paragraph no.25 of her cross- examination that the statements given by her to the police, as well as to the Magistrate, were not true, and the same were given under the influence of her parents.
She further deposed in cross- examination that she was 18 years of age on the date of incident.

In this way, it can be inferred that the victim has changed her statements given in the court, from the ones given by her earlier under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. to the police and under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate.
Thus, there is inconsistency in the statements of the victim, as she changed her version from time to time.

sentences.text: In addition to this, there is gross contradiction in the evidence of PW-1, PW-4 and PW-6 regarding the date, time and place of recovery of victim.
PW-6, the Investigating Officer of the case,
even did not prepare the memo of recovery.

In this matter, the victim, after being allegedly kidnapped, was said to be kept in the house of one-Pawan, however, the said Pawan was neither examined in the court nor the statement of the Pradhan of that village was recorded nor any reasonable justification has been given by the I.O. for the said lapse.
14. Last, but not the least, the Medical Officer PW-3, who examined the victim, has not given any clear opinion regarding the commission of rape upon the victim.

Although, the vaginal swab, vaginal smear and clothes etc. of the victim, as well as the blood sample of accused, were sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory for the purpose of forensic examination, the report received from the Laboratory being Paper No. 55A/1 to 55A/3 is on record, from a perusal of which also, the fact of commission of rape is not proved.

15. On the basis of aforesaid reasons, the trial Court did not find it a fit case to record the conviction,
and it, accordingly, recorded findings of acquittal.
16. We are in full agreement with the findings recorded by the trial Court and we find no reasonable ground to interfere with the well reasoned judgment passed by the trial court.

17. Even otherwise, it is trite law that when two views are possible, one pointing towards the guilt of the accused and the other towards his innocence, the one which is favourable to the accused must be adopted.
18. In view of the foregoing discussion, we do not find it a fit case to grant leave to appeal to the State.
Accordingly, the application seeking leave to appeal is rejected.
19. Resultantly, the Government appeal preferred by the State, is also dismissed.
20. Let a copy of this judgment and order alongwith LCR be sent back to the Court concerned for information.

(Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 20.07.2023 PN/-
